title: Insect Juvenile Hormones and Plant Juvenoids: Is There a Hidden Chemical Conversation?
content: Juvenile hormones (JHs) and ecdysteroids constitute the principal hormonal regulators in insects, with JHs playing a critical role in delaying metamorphosis and regulating development. Plant secondary metabolites can either mimic (agonists or “phytojuvenoids”) or antagonize (antagonists or anti JH agents) JH signalling, which highlights the hidden chemical conversation between plant defence and insect endocrinology. In this review, more than 30 JH-active phytochemicals have been identified and classified into functional categories, acting through distinct molecular mechanisms: agonists bind weakly the Met/Tai receptor complex, antagonists inhibit heterodimerization, and precocenes are allatotoxic, irreversibly damaging the corpora allata. Recent advances (such as in planta engineered biosynthesis of JH III) underscore the evolutionary parallelism of MVA-derived terpenoids in both plants and insects. However, critical research gaps arise from limited receptor-binding affinity studies, toxicokinetic profiling, and species-specific sensitivity. Future perspectives were also integrated by the examination of plant–insect interactions and suggesting systematic screening methodologies, such as the two-hybrid β-galactosidase assay, to guide the identification and characterization of novel JH-active phytochemicals.
